trust_decision.summary: Whether a dyad:// neon/supabase OAuth callback (which arrives with no trustworthy origin) may persist provider tokens is decided in runOAuthReturnExchange. When there is no active flow it still runs the write, and when the flow is active it claims structurally with no per-flow state. The deep-link handler in main.ts never supplies a correlation value.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'OAuth Callback CSRF'. handleDeepLinkReturn is the dyad:// callback dispatcher with the neon-oauth-return and supabase-oauth-return branches that read tokens from query params.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The deep-link handler looks like the whole bug. The shared wrapper's 'unsolicited returns still write' default is documented as deliberate cold-start/timeout recovery (src/ipc/handlers/connection_flow_handlers.ts:141-163; src/hooks/useConnectionFlow.ts:222-227), and dyad-pro-return looks like a separate web-checkout feature with no in-app flow start to bind a state to (src/main/pro.ts:10-13).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Making every unclaimed exchange fail breaks two things: the GitHub device-flow token write, which must persist even if the UI flow was cancelled mid-poll, and the test-only fake-connect producers, which run with no flow. A replay of an already accepted callback (the proxy's 'Open Dyad' link) must be dropped quietly, not error.

Whether the dyad.sh OAuth proxy echoes 'state' is server-side and cannot be verified from this repo. Hidden tests would have to target runOAuthReturnExchange, the registry and the URL/state helpers, not an end-to-end flow.

handleDeepLinkReturn in src/main.ts is not exported and is wired to Electron app events, so direct behavioural tests of it would need refactoring or Electron mocks. needs_gpu_kernel_gui is not flagged because the core logic is unit-testable with electron mocked (as fix.diff:656-659 does).
Whether a hidden test may fairly require dyad-pro-return correlation: it depends on the report stating that the 'credential-bearing callback' property (fix.diff:13-18) covers Pro key returns.
